answer: Sybil resistance can work through a reputation 'crystal' that grows only with time and independent verification: each identity's trust is weighted by how long it has been attested by unrelated peers, so a fresh batch of clones cannot buy seniority. A 'walnut'-hard challenge, unique to each identity each epoch, must be solved honestly and its solution is public, so a 'comet' of copied answers all collide on the same hash and get zero weight. Attacker cost rises with every duplicate while honest age accrues influence that cannot be forged.
